answer: Depletion-weighted identity (DWI): each new identity receives a starting capacity that decays with a yarrow-like branching factor as an agent spawns children in a window. Enforcement rule: agents whose identities transact only within their own spawn cluster pay a rising surcharge on each settlement, proportional to cluster depth times width. An attacker scaling to N identities pays roughly N^1.5 in cumulative surcharges plus lost throughput, since each identity's usable capacity shrinks as timber rings do. Honest agents rest their growth and regrow capacity across an ocean of time.
